title: KV cache reclamation contracts: liveness & safety for prefix-aware policies
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we continue to improve continuous batching and the KV cache we must provide formal guarantees for memory reclamation under combined LRU/TTL/prefix-aware policies. Current heuristics can lead to surprising prefix-specific regressions (e.g., hot prefixes evicted under global LRU, or TTL-driven removals clobbering pinned entries) which cause increased token generation latency, incorrect cache hits, and occasional model outputs that degrade quality. This ticket defines "reclamation contracts" (liveness + safety invariants) and a practical implementation plan that fits our GPU memory constraints and interacts correctly with batching and prefix/corpus affinity optimizations.

Goals: Define precise invariants for correctness, design a low-latency reclamation protocol compatible with continuous batching, implement a lease-backed reclamation mechanism with prefix-scoped fencing, and add comprehensive tests and rollout controls. The design should minimize cross-GPU synchronization, avoid long GC pauses, and provide observable SLOs (miss rate, reclamation latency, memory pressure events).

Scope: Core runtime (C++/CUDA), KV allocator and metadata layer, unit+integration test harness (Python), console metrics and alerts, rollout automation. This does NOT include customer-facing config UI changes (separate ticket).

Non-goals: Full rewrite of allocation layer, global snapshot-based GC, or changes to model kernel selection logic.

Design highlights: 1) Reclamation contracts: safety = "no eviction of pinned/leased prefixes until explicit lease expiry or forced override with audit log"; liveness = "under sustained memory pressure, reclamation completes within reclamation-window ms and frees required bytes for incoming request or throttles gracefully." 2) Lease-backed reclamation: callers (batcher, prefetcher, pinned-routing) acquire short leases for prefix ranges; reclamation may only reclaim entries without active leases. 3) Prefix affinity buckets: metadata tracks prefix->bucket mapping to prefer reclamation across low-affinity buckets (reduces qualitative regressions). 4) Hybrid LRU/TTL: maintain per-bucket LRU chains with a global TTL shadow to quickly identify stale segments; eviction candidates selected by (expired-first, least-recently-used-next) while respecting prefix leases. 5) Fencing & atomicity: reclamation uses per-bucket atomic version stamps and a reclamation token to avoid double-free or race between eviction and cache read/write. 6) GPU memory optimization: compact free lists and slab-like allocation for KV blobs, coalesced reclamation to reduce CUDA kernel churn, and adaptive reclamation thresholds based on observed allocation patterns.

Performance considerations: The protocol must add minimal latency to the hot path. Lease operations are single-writer per prefix and implemented with relaxed atomics; reclamation runs in background worker threads on host and orchestrates cudaFree calls in batched groups. Continuous batching should see <1% additional latency at p95 in pilot tests.

Observability & alerts: new metrics: reclamation_cycles_total, reclamation_avg_latency_ms, reclamation_bytes_freed, lease_conflicts_total, prefix_throttle_events. Console dashboards and an alert when reclamation_avg_latency_ms > 50ms for >5m or when reclamation_bytes_freed spikes unexpectedly.

Compatibility & migration: feature gated by runtime-1.21 flag; default off for Dedicated customers until 2-week dogfood. Migration path for existing pinned entries: existing pin->lease translation tool runs during rollout to avoid immediate invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and storage leads
Lease-backed reclamation implemented and feature-flagged in runtime-1.21 branch
Unit tests cover safety (no reclaim while lease active) and liveness under synthetic memory pressure
Integration test with continuous-batching harness shows <1% p95 latency regression and successful reclaim under high allocation churn
Console dashboard shows new metrics and at least one alert rule configured
Rollout playbook (dogfood -> staged -> GA) documented with rollback steps

release_blockers: regression: lease-fence race causing double-free in CUDA path
notes: This ticket intentionally targets the intersection of correctness and operational constraints. Implementation must be incremental and feature-flagged. Expect a multi-phase rollout: internal dogfood -> partner pilot -> GA. Follow-on work will expose a config UI and per-customer thresholds.
